name: Quadratic formula (x₁)
description: Returns one root x₁ of the quadratic equation ax²+bx+c=0 using (−b+√(b²−4ac))/(2a). This is the root taking the plus sign of the square root.
notes: Requires a≠0. If the discriminant b²−4ac is negative the roots are complex and this real formula does not apply.

name: Percentage (part ÷ whole)
description: Expresses the part as a percentage of the whole, computing part÷whole×100. The result tells you what share of the total the part represents.
notes: The whole must be nonzero. Result is a percentage, so 0.5 as a fraction here would be entered as part and whole values, not as 50.

name: Power (base^exp)
description: Raises base to the power of exponent, computing base^exponent. The exponent may be negative or fractional, giving reciprocals or roots respectively.
notes: A negative base with a fractional exponent may be undefined for real numbers. A zero base with a negative exponent is undefined (division by zero).

name: Logarithm (log_base x)
description: Computes the logarithm of x in an arbitrary base, using ln(x)÷ln(base). The result is the exponent to which the base must be raised to obtain x.
notes: Requires x>0, base>0 and base≠1. The default base is 10 (common logarithm); set base to e for the natural logarithm.

name: Quadratic formula (x₂)
description: Computes one root of the quadratic equation a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero using the minus branch of the quadratic formula: negative b minus the square root of the discriminant, all over two a. The result is that root x2.
notes: If the discriminant b squared minus 4ac is negative the root is not real, and a must be nonzero. This branch gives one of two roots; the plus branch gives the other.

name: Discriminant
description: Calculates the discriminant of a quadratic equation, b squared minus four times a times c. Its sign tells how many real roots the equation has: positive gives two, zero gives one, and negative gives none.
notes: A zero discriminant means a repeated (double) real root; a negative value means the two roots are complex conjugates. The coefficient a must be nonzero for a quadratic.

name: Arithmetic sequence (nth term)
description: Gives the nth term of an arithmetic sequence by adding (n minus 1) common differences d to the first term a1. The result is the value of the term at position n.
notes: The term index n should be a positive integer, and the common difference d is the fixed step added between consecutive terms; a negative d makes the sequence decrease.

name: Geometric sequence (nth term)
description: Computes the nth term of a geometric sequence, where each term is the previous one multiplied by the common ratio r. Starting from the first term a1, it returns a1 times r raised to the power (n minus 1).
notes: Term numbering starts at 1, so the first term uses n=1 and gives a1 (r to the power 0). A ratio between 0 and 1 shrinks the terms, while a negative r makes them alternate in sign.

name: Exponential growth
description: Computes a quantity growing exponentially at constant rate r per period, using a×(1 + r)^t from an initial value a over time t. Each period multiplies the value by the factor (1 + r).
notes: Enter r as a decimal per period, so 3 percent is 0.03. Time t and the rate must use the same period; a negative r would instead represent decay.

name: Exponential decay
description: Computes the amount remaining after exponential decay, using a×e^(−k·t) from initial amount a with decay constant k over time t. Larger k or longer t leaves less of the substance.
notes: The decay constant k relates to half-life by k = ln(2)/half-life; make sure k and t use the same time unit. The result approaches but never reaches zero.

name: Half-life remaining amount
description: Computes how much of an initial amount a remains after elapsed time t, given a half-life h, using a×0.5^(t/h). The quantity halves once for every interval of length h that passes.
notes: The elapsed time t and half-life h must share the same time unit. After one half-life half remains, after two a quarter, and so on.

name: Doubling time
description: Computes how long it takes for a quantity to double when growing at a constant per-period rate r, using ln(2)/ln(1 + r). The result is expressed in the same periods used for the rate.
notes: Enter r as a decimal per period, so 7 percent is 0.07. This is the exact formula; the Rule of 72 is only an approximation of it.

name: Linear interpolation
description: Estimates the y-value at a query point x on the straight line through two known points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), using y1 + (x−x1)(y2−y1)/(x2−x1). It reads a value linearly between two data points.
notes: The two x-values must differ so the slope is defined. Choosing an x outside the range from x1 to x2 extrapolates rather than interpolates.

name: Percent error
description: Computes the percent error of a measured value o relative to the actual value a, using abs((o−a)/a)×100. It expresses the size of the discrepancy as a percentage of the true value.
notes: The absolute value makes the result non-negative regardless of whether the measurement is high or low. It is undefined when the actual value a is zero.

name: Percent change
description: Computes the percentage change from an initial value a to a final value b, using (b−a)/a×100. A positive result means an increase and a negative result means a decrease.
notes: The change is measured relative to the initial value a, which must not be zero. Unlike percent error, the sign is kept to show direction.

name: Change base to natural log ratio
description: Computes the base-2 logarithm of x via the change-of-base formula ln(x)/ln(2). The result is the power to which 2 must be raised to obtain x.
notes: The input x must be positive. The same pattern, dividing ln(x) by ln(base), converts a natural log into a logarithm of any other base.

name: Relative error
description: Computes the relative error of a measured value against the true value as |measured - actual| / |actual|. It expresses the size of the error as a fraction of the true magnitude.
notes: The result is a fraction; multiply by 100 for a percentage. Undefined when the actual value is zero, and it can be misleading for true values very close to zero.

name: Logarithm power rule (base 10)
description: Applies the logarithm power rule in base 10: log(x^p) = p*log(x). It computes the base-10 logarithm of x raised to the power p by multiplying log(x) by the exponent p.
notes: The argument x must be positive. The exponent p may be any real number; log here denotes the base-10 logarithm, not the natural log.

name: Logarithm product rule (base 10)
description: Applies the logarithm product rule in base 10: log(a*b) = log(a) + log(b). It computes the base-10 logarithm of the product a*b as the sum of the individual logarithms.
notes: Both a and b must be positive for the logarithms to be defined. log denotes the base-10 logarithm; the identity holds for any logarithm base.

name: Half-life amount
description: Computes the remaining amount after exponential decay by half-life, a0*(1/2)^(t/h), where a0 is the initial amount, t the elapsed time and h the half-life. The quantity halves each time t increases by one half-life.
notes: Time t and half-life h must use the same time unit. The result carries the same unit as a0; over one half-life the amount drops to exactly half.

name: Continuous growth
description: Computes the value of a quantity under continuous exponential growth, p*exp(r*t), where p is the principal or initial amount, r the continuous rate and t the time. It gives the amount after continuous compounding.
notes: The rate r is a decimal per unit time (0.05 means 5 percent), and r and t must share the same time unit. A negative r models continuous decay.

name: Quadratic Function Vertex (x-coordinate)
description: Computes the x-coordinate of the vertex (the axis of symmetry) of the parabola y = ax² + bx + c, using x = −b/(2a).
notes: a must not be zero (otherwise the function is not quadratic). This x-value marks the parabola's minimum if a>0, or its maximum if a<0.

name: Quadratic Function Vertex (y-value)
description: Computes the y-value at the vertex of the parabola y = ax² + bx + c — its minimum value if a>0 or maximum value if a<0 — using y = c − b²/(4a).
notes: a must not be zero. Pair with the vertex x-coordinate formula x = −b/(2a) to get the full vertex point.

name: Logarithm Quotient Rule
description: Computes log₁₀(a/b) directly from a and b, illustrating the logarithm quotient rule log(a/b) = log(a) − log(b).
notes: Both a and b must be positive. log here means base-10 (common) logarithm, not the natural log.

name: Square of a Sum (Expansion)
description: Computes (a+b)² by expanding it into its three algebraic terms a² + 2ab + b², the basic identity for expanding a squared binomial.
notes: Equivalent to computing (a+b)^2 directly; this form shows the expanded terms explicitly, as taught in junior-high algebra.

name: Linear Recurrence Solution via Characteristic Root
description: Computes the n-th term of a linear recurrence sequence defined by a[k+1] = p·a[k] + q, using the closed-form solution derived from the characteristic equation. The result represents the value of the sequence at the given term index n.
notes: Requires p ≠ 1; when p = 1 the sequence is arithmetic and this formula is undefined (division by zero). The formula assumes n ≥ 1 with a1 as the first term.

name: nth Term via Difference Sequence (Arithmetic Differences)
description: Computes the n-th term of a sequence whose difference sequence b_n = a[n+1] − a[n] is itself arithmetic, given the first terms of both sequences and the common difference of the differences. The result represents the value of the original sequence at index n.
notes: Valid for n ≥ 1; the formula correctly reduces to a1 when n = 1. Here b1 is the first term of the difference sequence (b1 = a2 − a1).

name: Percentage of a number
description: Computes a given percentage of a number, using number×percent/100. For example 20 percent of 150 gives 30.
notes: Enter the percentage as a plain number (e.g. 20 for 20%), not as a fraction. The result is in the same unit as the input number.
